issues.legal_issue: An unregistered sale deed may be admitted as evidence of a contract in a suit for specific performance, but not as evidence of a completed sale.
material_facts: The plaintiff brought a suit for specific performance and tendered an unregistered sale deed as evidence of the alleged agreement to sell.
The trial court refused to admit the deed solely because it was unregistered.
The deed concerned immovable property and was of a kind requiring compulsory registration.
issues.conclusion: The deed was admissible under the proviso to Section 49 of the Registration Act, 1908, as evidence of a contract in the suit for specific performance, and the trial court was required to mark it for that limited purpose rather than treat it as evidence of a completed sale.
issues.legal_principle: Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908 requires registration of specified instruments, including instruments effecting sales of immovable property of the relevant value. Although Section 49 generally prevents an unregistered instrument from affecting immovable property or being received as evidence of a transaction affecting it, its proviso permits such an instrument to be received as evidence of a contract in a suit for specific performance, or of a qualifying collateral transaction. The deed may therefore be admitted as evidence of the contract, but not to prove a completed sale. K.B. Saha and Sons Private Limited v. Development Consultant Limited (2008) 8 SCC 564 sets out the principles governing the limited use of unregistered documents and supports adding that such a document may be evidence of a contract in a specific-performance suit. Kalavakurti Venkata Subbaiah v. Bala Gurappagari Guruvi Reddy (1999) 7 SCC 114 recognises that a specific-performance suit is wider than a proceeding seeking only registration. Section 3(b) of the Specific Relief Act, 1963 does not displace the proviso to Section 49 because admitting the deed for this limited purpose is consistent with the Registration Act.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking enforcement of an agreement to sell.
predicates.unregistered_sale_deed_tendered_as_contr: A party tendered an unregistered sale deed as evidence of the alleged contract to sell.
predicates.instrument_requires_compulsory_registrat: The instrument concerns a transaction for which the law requires registration.

issues.definition: When a party tenders an unregistered sale deed as evidence of a contract in a suit seeking enforcement of an agreement to sell, and the instrument requires compulsory registration, the deed may be admitted as evidence of the contract.
